method: Each row is one jurisdiction's statute book: its Acts in force laid end to end, each as wide as its pages (pages of text of 2,600 characters, the same unit in every row; printed pages are not, so the statute maps' printed figures for Singapore and Western Australia are not used). Subsidiary legislation is left out. The Acts Commons holds are drawn one by one; the rest are one block, from the researched count of Acts in force and their pages, less the Acts held. An Act's encoded share is the share of its deposited sections that some encoding covers: measured section by section by the statute maps for Singapore, the Commonwealth, Western Australia and New Zealand; elsewhere read from the deposited text and each encoding's scope, an estimate; an encoded Act whose share cannot be found is shown at 2%. Held Acts with no deposited text are drawn at the jurisdiction's average Act length.
act_columns: pages basis 2 a PDF's pages|1 pages of text|0 no text, jurisdiction average

keys.generated: the date the data was built
keys.ref_pages_per_act: the reference length of an Act, in pages (see world_map.py)
keys.method: how the rows are built, in a few sentences
keys.act_columns: the columns of each held Act in a jurisdiction's 'a'
keys.j: one entry per jurisdiction, in region order, each subdivision after its country: c code, n name, r region, p parent code or null, page 1 if legalese.com/commons/<c> exists, a the held Acts (act_columns), rest the Acts Commons does not hold, se the encoded subsidiary instruments held (not drawn)
keys.rest: acts and pages not held (acts in page-equivalents where the count is of code divisions), ab and pb the bases of the counts behind them, cf the research's confidence, est 1 where either is an estimate
